Read the settings a mapper recorded on its output

Source: R/scrutiny-meta.R
scrutiny_meta.Rd

Every mapper, such as grim_map(), records the settings of the call that produced its output. scrutiny_meta() returns them as a tibble, so that a report can state the rounding method or SD convention behind a result.

Settings are the arguments that apply to the whole call, with defaults resolved, such as rounding, x_meaning, or sd_meaning. Arguments that may vary by row, such as digits_x and items_averaged, are columns of the output instead, even if given as a single value. Sequence and total-n mappers, such as grim_map_seq(), add their own settings, such as dispersion.

Printed output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), debit_map(), or percentage_of_map(), including sequence and total-n output, has a header line that names the settings that are not at their defaults, as in # GRIM: rounding = "up", or says default settings.

Some dplyr verbs, such as summarise(), drop the record, and with it the header line; filter(), arrange(), and mutate() keep it.

Usage

scrutiny_meta(data)

Arguments

data

Output of a mapper function.

Value

A tibble with one row per setting and these columns, or NULL if data has no record of its settings:

  • setting: the name of the argument.

  • value: its value, written as R code, such as 'up' or 1:5.

  • default: TRUE if the value is the mapper's default, FALSE if not.

  • added_by: the mapper whose argument it is, such as "grim_map" or "grim_map_seq".

Examples

pigs1 |>
  grim_map(
    digits_x = 2,
    items_averaged = 1,
    data_type = "integer",
    rounding = "up"
  ) |>
  scrutiny_meta()
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   setting   value  default added_by
#>   <chr>     <chr>  <lgl>   <chr>   
#> 1 x_meaning 'mean' TRUE    grim_map
#> 2 rounding  'up'   FALSE   grim_map
#> 3 threshold 5      TRUE    grim_map
#> 4 symmetric FALSE  TRUE    grim_map
#> 5 show_rec  FALSE  TRUE    grim_map

# Only the settings that are not at their defaults:
pigs1 |>
  grim_map_seq(
    digits_x = 2,
    items_averaged = 1,
    data_type = "integer",
    dispersion = 1:10
  ) |>
  scrutiny_meta() |>
  dplyr::filter(!default)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   setting    value default added_by    
#>   <chr>      <chr> <lgl>   <chr>       
#> 1 dispersion 1:10  FALSE   grim_map_seq
